name: ai_allied_skill
purpose_es: La IA de tu bando pelea mejor y el enemigo queda exactamente igual. Tus soldados IA (tu escuadra, las escuadras IA aliadas con sus líderes, las guarniciones y las estáticas de tu bando) detectan antes y desde más lejos, reaccionan y avisan al grupo más rápido, tienen más valor, recargan más rápido y apuntan algo más rápido; la puntería sube poco, solo hasta la del mejor soldado enemigo. Por defecto, además, sus grupos IA nunca huyen, igual que los defensores de los pueblos. 'Tu bando' es el de cualquier jugador humano y se detecta solo. Dos opciones nuevas en el lobby, justo debajo de 'AI: Skill (all AI units)': 'VIOC: Habilidad de la IA de tu bando' (Igual que el enemigo / Un poco mejor / Mejorada, por defecto / Elite) y 'VIOC: La IA de tu bando nunca huye' (Sí por defecto). No cambia 'AI: Skill' ni el precio de 1/100 que paga la IA.
source: workflow vio_ai: research in work/vio_ai/ (mission_ai_map.md, skill_values.md, ai_mods.json), implementation 2026-10-13; notes in work/vio_ai/implementation_notes.md
reviewed: revisado 2026-10-13 (revisor SQF): sin errores de script; cada ancla aparece 1 vez en las 10 fuentes del catalogo y el dry-run de los 23 escenarios pasa. Corregido en esta version: la marca 'vioc_ally' guarda la propia unidad (un lider reaparecido se vuelve a procesar), 'nunca huye' se repite en cada pasada (cubre refuerzos y lideres nuevos) y aimingSpeed usa 'general' como piso.
risks: Human side = every side (west/east only) with a living human in allPlayers, re-checked every sweep and on each CreateUnit; a side that once had a human keeps the boost for the session; resistance and civilians are never touched, players are never touched. In the invasion scenarios the user may pick EAST, which then gets the boost on top of the catalog EAST economy bonus. Per-level raw targets come from work/vio_ai/skill_values.md (levels 2 and 3 exactly; level 1 is the midpoint between the enemy mean 0.40 and level 2), with +-0.05 jitter, applied as max(target, the unit's previous value) and capped at 1, so raising lobby 'AI: Skill' never lowers allies (at 50%+ the accuracy edge disappears, the spotting edge stays). All subskills are read before any is written because setSkill ['general', x] may propagate to subskills that were not set explicitly. CTI_AI_SKILL_BASE, CTI_AI_SKILL_SPAN and the BIS_fnc_EXP_camp_setSkill call are untouched, so the enemy and the AI 1/100 purchase price (Server_HandleAIPurchase.sqf, base < 0.40) do not change; the enemy slot leaders keep the EXP nerf (0.255/0.217 raw). The script is appended to init.sqf without an isServer guard on purpose: setSkill and allowFleeing need a local argument, so each machine handles only its local units (a dedicated server's clients would handle their own bought squad); on the user's hosted game everything is local to the host. It starts after CTI_Server_Loaded, so units created before that, and units not made by CTI_CO_FNC_CreateUnit (playable slot leaders, MP engine-respawned leaders, BIS_fnc_spawnVehicle UAV and SAM/radar crews, workers) are caught by the 20 s sweep (each unit body once: flag 'vioc_ally' stores the unit itself, so a respawned body is processed again even if Arma copies the old unit's variables to it). allowFleeing 0 (lobby switch, default on) is re-applied on every sweep to each local AI group of a human side that contains no player, so reinforcements that join later and respawned leaders are covered within 20 s; those groups never retreat from hopeless fights, like the town defenders; workers and independent salvagers are CARELESS, so no visible change there. Lobby params are read by index in Init_Parameters.sqf and nothing uses hardcoded paramsArray indices, so inserting two classes before 'class SEPERATOR_BASE {' is safe. Common_CreateUnit.sqf and Parameters.hpp use CRLF (apply_steps converts). aimingSpeed uses the unit's 'general' value as its keep-higher floor, because its CfgAISkill curve (0.5 + 0.5x) is not identity and 'skill' may return the converted value. Not verified in game: the skillFinal numbers (model in work/vio_ai/skillfinal_model.py).
test_in_game_es: En el lobby (PARAMETERS), debajo de 'AI: Skill (all AI units)', deben salir 'VIOC: Habilidad de la IA de tu bando' = 'Mejorada (recomendado)' y 'VIOC: La IA de tu bando nunca huye' = 'Si (recomendado)'. Deja 'AI: Skill' en 30%. Ya en la partida, después de 30 s: Escape -> consola de depuración, escribe VIOC_ALLY_STATUS y pulsa 'Ejecución local' (LOCAL EXEC): debe dar algo como [2,true,[WEST],N,M] con N y M mayores que 0. Para ver tu escuadra pega (units group player - [player]) apply {[name _x, (round (100*(_x skillFinal "spotDistance")))/100, (round (100*(_x skillFinal "aimingAccuracy")))/100]} y pulsa 'Ejecución local': con 'Mejorada' y dificultad Experto, unos 0.80-0.86 y 0.54-0.61. Mirando a un enemigo cercano: [cursorTarget skillFinal "spotDistance", cursorTarget skillFinal "aimingAccuracy"] debe dar unos 0.50-0.64 y 0.43-0.58, igual que antes. En combate: tus escuadras IA deberían ver y disparar primero más a menudo y ya no salir corriendo.

steps.text: if (!isNil "VIOC_fnc_allySkill") then {[_unit] call VIOC_fnc_allySkill}; //--- VIOC: IA de tu bando mas habil (parche ai_allied_skill, ver VIOC_ai_allies.sqf)

//--- VIOC: IA de tu bando mas habil y sin huir (copia configurada; parametros de lobby VIOC_AI_ALLY_SKILL y VIOC_AI_ALLY_NOFLEE; corre en cada maquina y solo toca sus unidades locales)
[] execVM "VIOC_ai_allies.sqf";
